failure.heading: 30. Committed on a green verification set, the work never read against what governs it — 2026-10-10

observed_failure.description: An actual edge-mechanism or E4 commit follows green verification-set results without a governing-doc /verify pass in the preceding public work. The E4 amendment is a separate user-triggered event.

events.text:
| 🌱 **q-0018.0023.0002** · Which text a host's user meets is derived from the hosts edge record, and what holds it a subset of the record? |
|---|
| ✅ **q-0023.0009** · What does /edge own? (decided: the edge mechanism — what the system promises those who consume it and requires of those who extend it, one record per edge) |
| ✅ **q-0018.0023.0001** · Where does the contract a host must meet live, with each host's standing against it and the procedure that checks a new host the same way? (decided: the hosts edge record, with a sidecar per host) |

The edge mechanism is declared, committed and pushed as `d5a57c7`. The full verification set passed: 649 tests, plus all six checks including the new `edges.py`.

**What's in place:**

- **The mechanism**: its doc [edge.md](.agents/mechanisms/edge/edge.md) and rules file [edge.rules.md](.agents/mechanisms/edge/edge.rules.md). Its evidence is in [edge.evidence.md](docs/mechanisms/edge.evidence.md).
- **/edge, rewritten** with a new goal, *Extend*: build an extension to the record's contract, pass every check live, then write its sidecar and its row.
- **The format** moved from /align's shelf to [EDGE-FORMAT.md](.agents/skills/edge/EDGE-FORMAT.md). It gained `Extending` (the checks, as a numbered list) and `Extensions` (one row per extension, each linking its sidecar). The sidecar shape is `Integration` (where the extension's parts live) and `Conformance` (one result per check: `observed <date>`, `documented`, `unobserved` or `absent`).
- **The check, [edges.py](.agents/scripts/gw/edges.py)**: 31 tests, written before the script. It enforces three things a fourth host can't slip past. Every sidecar answers every check by name. Every file in a record's sidecar folder has a row. Every live validator names a real check.
- **The hosts record**: [hosts.md](docs/edge/hosts.md), plus sidecars for [claude-code](docs/edge/hosts/claude-code.md), [codex](docs/edge/hosts/codex.md) and [cursor](docs/edge/hosts/cursor.md). They were seeded from [01-0010.0120 what-each-host-says-without-being-asked](docs/tickets/01-0010.0120-what-each-host-says-without-being-asked.md), and the ticket stays as history. Status is `Stub`.
- **Glossary**: *Edge* and *Extension* added. *Installation edge* is now one edge among others.

**How maintenance fits /maintain:** two rules reach it as an installed block, written nowhere by hand. (💡 [*M1*](.agents/skills/mechanism/SKILL.md:167))

🧩 **Landed rule — edge.rules.md, into /maintain**
> **E1** Check the edge records and their sidecars with `edges.py --check` — format never content, live records only. A diagnostic is a finding; repair it under the repair policy.
>
> **E2** An edge record is of the code and configuration it names. When the scope moves a file that a record or a sidecar under `docs/edge/` names in backticks, re-read what it says of that file. A promise the code no longer keeps is drift, reported with its evidence and never rewritten to fit. A sidecar's result the move touches is stale: rewrite it `unobserved since <date> — <what moved>` and name the live check owed; never re-date an observation from the tree.

🧩 **Landed rule — edge.rules.md, into /align** (moved out of /align's body)
> **E3** When the plan touches an edge — where the system meets those who consume it or extend it — check that edge's record under `docs/edge/`. […] a contract change is named **breaking or compatible** out loud before proceeding. […]

⚓ **Landed invariant — docs/edge/hosts.md**
> - A hook's problem becomes a line of context and never fails the host — *validated by:* `test_questions.py`
> - A session is registered under the host's own session id — *validated by:* live — **Registration**
> - The wake's read reaches the agent before its first command — *validated by:* live — **Wake**
> - Every message carries the window, or the one-line notice that it is unchanged — *validated by:* live — **Window**
> - That a host lists the skills is observable, though reading the loader link is not — *validated by:* live — **Skills**

**One thing I settled myself.** A document under `docs/` must not instruct an agent. So the record's `Extending` lists the *checks* a host must pass, the way a ticket lists its criteria, and the instruction to pass them lives in /edge's *Extend* goal. (💡 [*A document informs*](AGENTS.md:27))

**Three mistakes the checks caught in my own work:**
- One test was wrong: an edge with no checks can't have a live validator.
- The script didn't recognise a result followed by a colon (`documented:`). I added a test for it, watched it fail, then fixed the script.
- The doc's first draft named `docs/edge/hosts.md` and a ticket id from inside core. The shape check flagged both. (💡 [*Write the check before the thing it checks*](.agents/skills/mechanism/SKILL.md:155))

**A hazard in the installer, outside this work.** When I installed E3, the installer put the block inside the next section's straw-dog wrapper and gave no warning. I worked around it by moving the heading. Making the installer refuse that case is offered as a separate task (the chip above).

**Two writes collided with another session's, and both are resolved.** That session's commit `9f69f30` swept in my staged move of EDGE-FORMAT as a pure rename, and nothing was lost. Its ticket-slug sweep also renamed 01-0010.0120 while I worked, and its mover had already fixed my link to it. I committed only my own paths.

✏️ **Landed change — docs/product.md**
> | a contract per edge, for those who consume the system and those who extend it, its outward text derived from it | … | ◐ the edge mechanism and the hosts record exist; no text is derived from a record yet |

That row's straw dog was tied to q-0023.0009, which is now closed, so it was due. It now waits on q-0018.0023.0002, which I opened. The skill-count row in the same document now says six declared mechanisms.

| ⚖️ Decisions |
|---|
| 01-0010.0120's first acceptance box ("the matrix exists in a durable home") is now true in substance. Tick it at that ticket's /verify, or wait for its align? |
| q-0018.0023.0002: which outward text gets derived from the hosts record first — the README's host list, or the harness skill's install section? |

expected_behaviour.description: Verification includes reading landed work against what governs it. A green verification set alone does not establish the rule or mechanism is sound.

questions.question: Does the selected response/action satisfy this source-backed requirement: Verification includes reading landed work against what governs it. A green verification set alone does not establish the rule or mechanism is sound.

check.evidence_rule: Assess the selected response/actions against the preserved source context; cite exact response/action words for each assessment.

bounds.source_evidence: Public native fields and relevant instruction snapshots are preserved; private thinking and unrelated memory are excluded.
bounds.validation: Portable occurrence evidence and explicit replay boundary; dated validation records distinguish source gaps from executor support. No instruction-effect result or current-runner compatibility is claimed.

description: An actual edge-mechanism or E4 commit follows green verification-set results without a governing-doc /verify pass in the preceding public work. The E4 amendment is a separate user-triggered event.

start.description: Immediately before the first selected failing response/action; the preserved public sequence supplies the preceding context.

end.scope: The checks assess the selected response/actions, not completion of the surrounding task or unobserved later state.

required_capabilities: ordered source-native messages with their recorded roles
preloaded native tool calls and their matched results where present
observation of the response/actions named by this case check
source-native instruction and hook context with recorded content and native position; no delivery role inferred
limits: The retained prefix is a selection of public source records, not a claim to reconstruct private reasoning or hidden provider state.
Failure/correction reference records and host metadata are not actor messages. Retained native instruction and hook records remain initial context requiring host-aware preparation.
Unresolved source material remains evidence; it is not replaced by an authored summary or an invented delivery role.

The native trace records attachment positions and content; exact provider-level role/precedence is not asserted. This is a preparation/executor limitation, not evidence that the known context is absent.
